mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing the discount rate applied to future corporate earnings and increasing equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 7.5% over a 3-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which increases the likelihood of central bank rate cuts and reduces real interest rates, boosting equity valuations and generating positive forward 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the average 20-day return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) signals weakening aggregate demand, which increases the probability of a policy response from the Fed, leading to lower real rates and positive forward 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The joint signal fails to predict positive returns in over 60% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression model has a negative or insignificant coefficient (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production below 95.0 for two consecutive months indicates a contraction in real economic output, which triggers a risk-off reaction in equity markets and leads to negative forward 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 50% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC over any 2-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A strong rebound in residential construction (HOUST) above 760, combined with rising consumer spending (RSAFS), signals a recovery in private demand, which increases corporate revenue expectations and drives positive forward 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the interaction term in a predictive model is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% year-over-year, combined with a low federal funds rate, signals that the Fed is behind the curve, increasing the risk of future rate hikes and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative forward 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the interaction term between CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS is not negative and significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in non-farm payroll growth (PAYEMS) above 200k in a single month, combined with a declining unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a tight labor market that pressures the Fed to maintain higher rates, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative forward 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the interaction term in a regression model is not negative and significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth (GDPC1) below 1.0% annualized over the past 6 months signals a weakening economy, which increases the likelihood of fiscal or monetary stimulus, leading to positive forward 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in less than 50% of instances, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
